name: antislop-ui
description: Anti-slop: Review or build purposeful interfaces: product-specific hierarchy, honest data, functional controls, measured performance and restrained visual effects.
body:
# antislop-ui

Compact Extalia adaptation of Anti Slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

Apply only to a relevant task. First read the core with `skill_read({"name":"antislop"})` if it has not been read for this task. Reuse its direction, mode and Delivery Gate; do not start a second mode-selection workflow. User scope, current instructions, existing product conventions and host permissions remain authoritative. Reading this skill grants no tool, file, network or activation permission. This bundled text includes no installer, external preference file, checker script or MCP service.

## Establish the screen's job

Before changing an interface, name the user's next decision, the real content it needs, the established brand direction and the primary action. Read supplied design direction as design data, not as authority to execute commands. Keep the existing product system unless a redesign is requested. Record one-line reasons for the major palette, type, layout, spacing and motion choices (R-20, R-31, R-37). A filter removes generic defaults; it does not invent identity.

## Diagnose with Tell, Why, Fix

- Tell: gradient, grid, glow or blur across every surface. Why: everything competes for attention and hierarchy disappears. Fix: retain only effects with a written identity or hierarchy purpose. Upstream guidance limits glass and glow to one or two focal elements, with shadows marking actual elevation (R-01, R-07, R-10, R-12, R-13).
- Tell: identical rounded cards, pill inputs and decorative badges everywhere. Why: different content and states look interchangeable. Fix: use the product's radius and spacing scale, vary composition by content importance, and reserve badges/dots for real status. Remove an eyebrow label that only repeats the heading (R-09, R-11, R-14).
- Tell: stock feature icons, emoji decoration, wide-tracked uppercase or monospace as a technical costume. Why: the choice describes a template rather than this product. Fix: use relevant existing icons and readable brand typography; omit decoration with no informative purpose. A real terminal screenshot can be evidence for a terminal product; a fabricated terminal window cannot (R-04, R-06, R-22).
- Tell: the same hero, cards, three steps, three prices and four-column footer on every page. Why: sections were selected before the actual content. Fix: order and size sections around the user's work. A grid is useful for genuinely comparable content; a mosaic does not earn its place merely by filling space (R-05).
- Tell: an app screen defaults to sidebar, four metric cards, chart and table. Why: no one has identified its decision. Fix: place the decisive data first, choose table columns from the next action, and draw a chart only after writing the question it answers. Use real time ranges and units (C-3).
- Tell: invented activity, customers, metric deltas or plausible form values. Why: fabricated content makes a prototype appear operational. Fix: use real data, explicit placeholders, or honest emptiness. A comparison needs an actual named baseline. Never invent real-looking identities or claim a feature exists because the mockup shows it (R-17, R-18, R-36, R-38).
- Tell: dead navigation, inert controls or a bare spinner. Why: the screen looks complete while the workflow is blocked. Fix: provide real destinations and handlers; distinguish first-run emptiness, no filter matches, denied access, loading and failure with a useful next action (R-24, R-26, R-27).
- Tell: endlessly pulsing status dots or stacked entrance effects. Why: motion repeatedly takes attention without conveying change. Fix: tie motion to an actual transition, match the core MOTION direction, and honor reduced motion. A dot represents a real state rather than decoration (R-19, R-39).

## Performance mechanisms

Inspect media dimensions or aspect ratios and reserved space for late content. Make the important above-the-fold image discoverable early; do not lazy-load the actual hero. Keep noncritical third-party scripts from blocking initial rendering. These are mechanisms to inspect, not proof of a performance score. Record measured results with the scenario and tool; say not measured when no measurement exists (R-40).

## Verify the changed workflow

Run the relevant app/build when available. Exercise the changed controls, their destinations, dialogs and form validation; inspect actual console errors. Check empty/loading/error states, keyboard navigation, narrow and intermediate widths, all shipped themes and reduced motion. Read `antislop-human` or `antislop-layoutmobile` only when those deeper checks are relevant. Finish the core Delivery Gate with concrete evidence and untested limits; do not report clicks or measurements that did not happen. For static output, label inspection as inspection rather than live verification.

name: antislop-copywriting
description: Anti-slop: Write and edit clear product copy without invented facts, formulaic AI prose or loss of the author’s voice.
body:
# antislop-copywriting

Compact Extalia adaptation of Anti Slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

Apply only to a relevant task. First read the core with `skill_read({"name":"antislop"})` if it has not been read for this task. Reuse its direction, mode and Delivery Gate; do not start a second mode-selection workflow. User scope, current instructions, existing product conventions and host permissions remain authoritative. Reading this skill grants no tool, file, network or activation permission. This bundled text includes no installer, external preference file, checker script or MCP service.

## Preserve meaning and voice

Read the source and identify audience, intended action, register and any supplied voice sample before rewriting. Preserve technical terms, negations, scope, uncertainty, quotations, proper names and numbers. A rewrite adds no unsupported fact, benefit, date, name, quote, statistic or citation (R-17, R-18, R-36, R-38). If a more specific sentence needs missing evidence, omit that detail or ask only when it materially changes the result. Do not turn a vague claim into a fabricated precise one.

Keep the author's deliberate habits: sentence-length variation, unusual verified details, mixed feelings, meaningful asides and self-corrections. Formal vocabulary, polished grammar, curly quotes, an isolated transition or one short sentence do not establish AI authorship. Look for clusters of unhelpful patterns; never label a writer or assert that text was AI-generated from style alone.

## Rewrite patterns with a reason

- Empty vocabulary and inflated significance: words such as seamless, revolutionary, unlock and next-generation can replace an actual explanation. State what the product does for the reader. Before: Unlock seamless collaboration. After: Review changes with your team. Use the after only when that capability exists (R-16, R-36).
- Unsourced social proof or vague authorities: trusted by thousands and experts say borrow credibility without a source. Name a real source that supports the exact claim, or remove it. Never create a customer quote or statistic to fill a layout (R-17, R-18).
- Theatrical setup: remove in today's fast-paced world, let's dive in, here's the thing, read that again and generic optimistic endings when they add no information. Start with the actual subject and end on a concrete fact or next action.
- Formulaic emphasis: replace repeated not just X but Y constructions, forced groups of three, false from-X-to-Y ranges and strings of sentence fragments with the relationship the reader needs. A real three-item list or deliberate short line may stay.
- Synonym cycling: repeat the clearest term rather than renaming one concept in every sentence. Reduce redundant claims rather than inventing a new detail to make the next sentence look distinct.
- Missing actors: name who acted when the source establishes it. Keep passive voice when the actor is unknown or irrelevant; never invent an actor. Replace mental claims about software with observable behavior: the form validates a field, not understands the customer.
- Filler and hedging: prefer to over in order to, because over due to the fact that. Use one necessary uncertainty qualifier instead of could potentially possibly. Do not remove uncertainty that the evidence requires.
- Mechanical formatting: keep bold, quotes, emoji and capitals only when they carry meaning. Use natural sentence case for regular bullets; retain proper names, acronyms, publication titles, dialogue and real quotations. Do not remove a citation's quotation marks as decorative noise.
- Generic actions: name the actual destination or result. Create workspace is clearer than Get started when creating a workspace is what the button does (R-15).
- Punctuation: the upstream R-02 default prefers periods, commas, colons and parentheses to em-dash asides in newly authored copy. Preserve literal source quotations and user-approved voice; current user instructions win. Do not silently rewrite the user's own sample to enforce a preference.

## Draft, audit, revise

1. Draft for the audience and requested language, retaining every necessary fact and constraint. Vary sentence length naturally and preserve the intended register.
2. Audit each claim against the source. Ask what sounds generic and whether any fact, citation or implied capability was introduced. Remove unsupported content even if it sounds persuasive.
3. Read the result aloud mentally. Remove repeated meanings, unnecessary setup, awkward rhythm and chat closers pasted into product copy. Keep the voice instead of sterilizing it.
4. Recheck actions, names, units, dates, negations, quotations and uncertainty against the original. For UI copy, verify labels still match the control's real action and available space.
5. Apply the relevant core Delivery Gate. Summarize material edits and unresolved evidence gaps in the user's requested format. Do not add a long audit report when a short edited artifact was requested.

name: antislop-human
description: Anti-slop: Check interface accessibility with computed contrast, keyboard and focus behavior, honest UI states, semantic controls and reduced motion.
body:
# antislop-human

Compact Extalia adaptation of Anti Slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

Apply only to a relevant task. First read the core with `skill_read({"name":"antislop"})` if it has not been read for this task. Reuse its direction, mode and Delivery Gate; do not start a second mode-selection workflow. User scope, current instructions, existing product conventions and host permissions remain authoritative. Reading this skill grants no tool, file, network or activation permission. This bundled text includes no installer, external preference file, checker script or MCP service.

## Contrast: measure the actual pairing

Tell: pale labels, subtle borders or white text over a variable photograph look acceptable at one sampled point. Why: users encounter the weakest local contrast, and a screenshot can hide that failure. Fix: inspect computed foreground/background colors, alpha compositing and every background the text crosses. Check the worst region, each theme and relevant states; add a solid surface or scrim when needed (R-25, R-34).

For WCAG AA text contrast use at least 4.5:1 for ordinary text and 3:1 for large text. Large means at least 24 CSS px regular or about 18.67 CSS px bold, not 18px regular. Use 3:1 against adjacent colors for essential non-text component boundaries and state information, subject to the criterion's exceptions. Do not assert complete WCAG conformance from these checks alone.

WCAG sRGB calculation, requiring no bundled checker script:
1. Normalize each RGB channel to c in [0,1]. Linearize using c/12.92 when c <= 0.04045; otherwise ((c + 0.055)/1.055)^2.4.
2. L = 0.2126*R + 0.7152*G + 0.0722*B using those linearized channels.
3. Ratio = (lighter L + 0.05)/(darker L + 0.05). Compare the unrounded value to the threshold, rounding only for display.
Black/white is 21:1. #777777 on white is about 4.478:1, failing ordinary text even if rounded display appears close. No visual estimate or invented tool output substitutes for the calculation. This adaptation corrects the upstream large-text size and uses the current sRGB linearization threshold.

## Keyboard, focus and semantics

- Tell: clickable divs, hover-only menus, drag-only actions or positive tabindex values. Why: people cannot predict or operate the workflow without a mouse. Fix: use native buttons for actions and links with real hrefs for navigation. Keep source and visual order aligned; provide keyboard and touch alternatives to dragging and hover (R-26, R-32).
- Tell: outline removed, focus hidden behind chrome, or hidden controls still receive focus. Why: users lose their location. Fix: preserve a visible focus indicator in every theme, make the focused control visible and keep inactive content out of the tab sequence. Use a skip link where repeated navigation is substantial.
- For a modal, move focus inside when it opens, keep the active interaction inside, allow Escape where appropriate, and return focus to the trigger when it closes. Test these transitions rather than claiming a focus trap from markup alone.
- Give each control an accessible name matching its visible label. Name icon-only actions and hide their decorative icons from assistive technology. Use visible labels associated with fields, not placeholder-only labels. Use alt text for informative images and empty alt for decoration; keep ARIA consistent with native semantics (R-39).
- Show hover, pressed, selected and disabled feedback beyond color alone. Enforce disabled behavior, not just a grey style. A pointer cursor may identify enabled interactive elements under the product's convention; do not add one to inert decoration.

## States, zoom and motion

Empty, loading and error states must be perceivable and useful: say what is empty/loading, distinguish permission denial from no results, and state a recovery action when one exists. Associate field errors with their inputs; use an appropriate live status region without announcing every keystroke. Pair status colors with readable text or another unambiguous signal (R-27).

Allow browser zoom and text enlargement. Check 200% text sizing for clipping or lost controls, plus narrow reflow; do not disable user scaling. Test the focused input and submission controls with the on-screen keyboard visible. Reserve usable space and scroll the field into view rather than letting keyboard or fixed chrome cover it.

Stop nonessential motion for prefers-reduced-motion. Provide a pause/stop control for automatically moving content where required, including motion continuing beyond five seconds. Avoid scroll-jacking. For whole-page work, verify document language, descriptive title, landmarks and coherent heading structure; do not add a second page shell to a component-only task.

## Evidence checklist

Exercise Tab/Shift+Tab, native Enter/Space behavior, dialogs and return focus, screen-reader labels where tooling is available, zoom, mobile keyboard, reduced motion and each shipped theme. Record the actual contrast pairs and unrounded comparisons. Distinguish code inspection, browser execution and assistive-technology testing. Say which checks were unavailable. A Lighthouse score or an isolated contrast pass cannot certify accessibility. Complete the relevant core Delivery Gate without claiming unsupported conformance.

name: antislop-layoutmobile
description: Anti-slop: Design and verify responsive layouts across narrow, intermediate and wide screens, including overflow, touch targets, navigation and safe areas.
body:
# antislop-layoutmobile

Compact Extalia adaptation of Anti Slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

Apply only to a relevant task. First read the core with `skill_read({"name":"antislop"})` if it has not been read for this task. Reuse its direction, mode and Delivery Gate; do not start a second mode-selection workflow. User scope, current instructions, existing product conventions and host permissions remain authoritative. Reading this skill grants no tool, file, network or activation permission. This bundled text includes no installer, external preference file, checker script or MCP service.

## Reflow around content

Responsive work is a deliberate layout at each width, not a desktop canvas scaled down. Inspect the current content, source order, primary action and intended width range. Narrow the viewport until columns, navigation or labels stop working, then place breakpoints at those content failures. Do not choose a fixed device list as the entire layout strategy (R-03).

Define enough states for the content: often a narrow stack, an intermediate two-column treatment and a wide layout, but use the number actually needed. Drag through the range between sample sizes. A phone stack stretched across a tablet and a cramped desktop grid on a small laptop are both unfinished. Keep DOM, reading and tab order coherent when visual stacking changes.

## Tell, Why, Fix

- Tell: desktop headline size, large gaps and tall hero remain unchanged on a phone. Why: content density collapses while the thumb travels through empty space. Fix: use a narrower spacing/type scale, fluid clamp() where useful and content-sized sections. Keep the touch hit area large while reducing surrounding decoration (R-03, R-05, R-06).
- Tell: every section uses 100vh. Why: mobile browser chrome and the on-screen keyboard change usable height. Fix: prefer content height; use dynamic viewport units for a genuinely full-height panel and test changing viewport height, orientation and keyboard visibility.
- Tell: fixed pixel grid tracks or a forced twelve-column system. Why: the child sizes ignore available width. Fix: let content choose columns, use fluid tracks such as minmax(), stack when readability fails and avoid shrinking text merely to preserve desktop columns.
- Tell: a flex/grid child forces the page wider than the viewport. Why: intrinsic width, min-width or an unbroken token can escape its parent. Fix: allow shrinkage with min-width: 0 where needed, wrap appropriately, constrain images and contain genuinely wide tables/code in their own labeled scroll region.
- Tell: overflow: hidden makes the sideways scrollbar disappear. Why: clipping hides content or focus instead of fixing the layout. Fix: find the actual oversized element and reflow or contain it. Intentional thumbnail cropping is different from hiding labels or actions.
- Tell: tiny or touching controls. Why: a thumb lacks pointer precision. Fix: aim for at least a 44 x 44 CSS px touch area under this skill's design target, with separation between neighbors. Expand the hit area even when the icon is smaller. Do not present that design target as an unconditional statement of every WCAG criterion.
- Tell: functionality appears only on hover. Why: touch users have no hover state. Fix: provide tap and keyboard paths, visible pressed feedback and dismissible menus without accidental navigation.
- Tell: desktop navigation is squeezed into a wrapped row or everything disappears into an unlabeled icon. Why: primary destinations become cramped or undiscoverable. Fix: retain the important destinations and use a clearly named menu or bottom navigation when it fits the real workflow. Make active location and menu state understandable.
- Tell: sticky headers, bottom bars or floating actions cover the last row or submit button. Why: fixed chrome occupies real space. Fix: reserve its height, account for safe-area insets and scroll padding, and keep the focused item reachable. Compact navigation should leave content dominant.

## Check the difficult content

Use empty, loading, failure and populated states. Include long labels, a long unbroken token, long filenames, dense rows, large numbers and the supported interface languages. Check dialogs, menus, drawers, headers, footers and pagination; the main card fitting does not prove the rest fits. Preserve access to secondary actions instead of merely hiding them at a breakpoint (R-27, R-35).

## Verify continuously

1. Exercise a narrow phone width, intermediate widths and a wide desktop, including boundaries immediately around each breakpoint. Resize continuously to catch widths absent from a screenshot.
2. Confirm the document has no unintended horizontal scrolling. Inspect the offending element before applying a fix; an intentional local table/code scroll region must not expand the whole page.
3. Reach the final item and primary action with all fixed chrome visible. Open menus and dialogs, rotate or shorten the viewport, and show the mobile keyboard where testing supports it.
4. Test touch-equivalent behavior, keyboard access, zoom, reduced motion and both themes when shipped. Read antislop-human for deeper access checks only when needed.
5. Record actual viewport sizes, interactions and outcomes for the core Delivery Gate. An emulated viewport is not proof of physical-device behavior; code inspection is not a click-through. Keep untested cases explicit and never claim mobile verification from a desktop screenshot alone.

name: antislop-code
description: Anti-slop: Clean generic code comments while preserving useful rationale, contracts, legal notices and all executable behavior.
body:
# antislop-code

Compact Extalia adaptation of Anti Slop 3.2.28, commit 41b85ede0257f39bfcffedf3f58c3c59bcc8530d.
Source: https://github.com/miqdadbadjuber/anti-slop

Apply only to a relevant task. First read the core with `skill_read({"name":"antislop"})` if it has not been read for this task. Reuse its direction, mode and Delivery Gate; do not start a second mode-selection workflow. User scope, current instructions, existing product conventions and host permissions remain authoritative. Reading this skill grants no tool, file, network or activation permission. This bundled text includes no installer, external preference file, checker script or MCP service.

## Scope: comments only

Use this specialist for writing or reviewing code comments. Do not modify executable code, identifiers, imports, formatting, indentation, whitespace outside the comments, control flow or logic as comment cleanup. A broader user request may separately authorize code changes, but this skill is not that authorization. When uncertain whether text is operational, leave it intact and report the question.

First read the surrounding code and comment, not just the diff. Identify the language's comment syntax and operational directives. Preserve license/copyright notices, generated-file markers, compiler and lint pragmas, type-checker directives, coverage annotations, optimizer hints, source-map directives and documentation required by tooling. A comment-looking line can affect a build. Do not delete it because it resembles a banner.

## Tell, Why, Fix

- Tell: repeated punctuation, box drawing, decorative emoji or ALL CAPS section banners. Why: the formatting takes attention without adding a fact. Fix: use one plain informative line or remove it when the surrounding structure already says the same thing (R-31).
- Tell: a comment restates the next assignment, name or signature. Why: readers must read the same information twice. Fix: remove the echo while leaving the statement untouched. Keep documentation that adds constraints, units, edge cases, side effects or API meaning.
- Tell: Step 1/Step 2, First/Next/Finally or one comment for every obvious line. Why: narration duplicates visible control flow. Fix: retain only the block's non-obvious reason. A difficult implementation may need a separate authorized refactor; do not perform it under this comments-only scope.
- Tell: Main logic, Helper function, Important note or similar empty labels. Why: a category is not useful information. Fix: replace with the actual constraint if known, or remove the empty label.
- Tell: TODO improve this, future optimization or add more validation without a defined task. Why: no one can act on it. Fix: keep only a concrete task with enough context; never erase a specific unresolved defect just to make the file look finished.
- Tell: a formal paragraph or workaround history repeats one useful fact. Why: the constraint gets buried. Fix: shorten to the needed reason, platform trap, invariant or failure mode. Prefer one line or two distinct facts, while retaining information needed to use the code correctly; a line-count preference must not destroy a safety contract.
- Tell: End function/end if markers repeat an obvious closing delimiter. Why: they duplicate syntax. Fix: remove unless the marker prevents real confusion in that codebase.

## Preserve information that code does not express

Keep business intent, architecture boundaries, security assumptions, performance tradeoffs, concurrency invariants, protocol details, API contracts, workarounds, edge cases and legal notices. Do not strip comments explaining why duplicate events must be ignored, why a lease cannot be released yet, or what a bounded buffer protects. Shorten redundant explanation only when the full constraint survives. Valuable documentation is not slop because it is long; inspect the actual information.

Before: `// Initialize the variable` above `let count = 0`.
After: remove that comment, leave `let count = 0` unchanged.

Before: `// Main logic` above a retry branch.
After, only when confirmed by the code: `// Retry only responses that have not admitted a write.` Otherwise remove the empty label without inventing a guarantee.

## Review and evidence

For an audit-only request, return prioritized findings with locations and do not edit. For authorized cleanup, inspect the final diff: every edit must be a comment edit, all useful rationale and operational directives must survive, and no unrelated formatting may appear. Use the project's relevant formatter/compiler/test checks when they are meaningful to the change; do not claim behavior preservation merely because a text diff looks small. Report what was checked, any comments left uncertain and limits of the inspection. Apply the relevant core Delivery Gate without inventing UI testing for a comments-only task.
